messages.author: 2a3b73736ea89ff6
messages.subject: Multicores on Apple's M1 chip
parts:
Hi INLA users,

I am currently using INLA to construct rgeneric models on my Macbook with Apple's M1 chip which has 8 cores. However, the INLA never uses multicores no matter how large the model is (NNGP models with 500-3000 locations). Does anyone else has this problem too? I am wondering if this is caused by the incompatibility of the CPU? BTW, the parallel package works well on my laptop. Thanks.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Multicores on Apple's M1 chip
parts:
Hi

can you verify running

demo(Leuk)

just interrupt when the plotting start, and then look at

result$logfile

you should see around line 600, something like

[597] "Compute corrected stdev for theta[3]: negative 1.034 positive 1.005"
[598] "maxld= -2527.581 fn=177 theta= 10.867 9.335 2.140 7.361 [10.5, 0.01]"
[599] "config 0/25=[ 0.000 0.000 0.000 0.000 ] log(rel.dens)= -0.003, [0] accept, compute, 0.02s"
[600] "config 1/25=[ 0.000 -0.000 0.000 2.210 ] log(rel.dens)= -2.449, [1] accept, compute, 0.02s"
[601] "config 2/25=[ 1.117 -1.270 1.156 -1.138 ] log(rel.dens)= -2.222, [3] accept, compute, 0.02s"
[602] "config 3/25=[ -0.516 0.909 -1.053 -1.138 ] log(rel.dens)= -2.015, [2] accept, compute, 0.02s"
[603] "config 4/25=[ 2.234 0.000 0.000 -0.000 ] log(rel.dens)= -2.477, [0] accept, compute, 0.02s"


the '[3]' is the thread number, so this runs with 4 threads.

If this does not happen, try to define number of threads manually,

inla.setOption(num.threads="4:1")

and rerun demo(Leuk)



the other explanation is the 'rgeneric', as linking with libR only allow one R-interpreter, so the R-part needs to be run in serial, so 
this, with smaller models take to much time that it does not look that its running in parallel, as that part will dominate. But that does not go well with serial for larger models. 


btw, I just got my iMac M1 yesterday, and we will be able to provide native builds on the M1 for future versions.

Best
H
